Part 2&3 事件 EVENTS

Describe a bicycle/motorcycle/car trip you would like to go

描述一次你想骑自行车/摩托车/开车去的小旅行

⚠️ AI 范例，仅供学习 — IELTS 口语全程独立完成，背诵照搬 AI 答案会被考官识别为背稿。

Part 2 话题卡片

Describe a bicycle/motorcycle/car trip you would like to go

  • Who you would like to go with (你想和谁一起去)
  • Where you would like to go (你想去哪里)
  • When you would like to go (你想什么时候去)
  • And explain why you would like to go by bicycle/motorcycle/car (并解释你为什么想骑自行车/摩托车/开车去)

问题与答案

Cue CardDescribe a bicycle/motorcycle/car trip you would like to go

I'd like to talk about a trip I would like to go on by car, which is something I've never actually experienced before. The person I'd like to go with is my girlfriend, because we both enjoy travelling together, and we've talked about this idea several times. As for where we'd go, we haven't decided on a specific destination yet. We've discussed a few options, like driving along the coast near Shenzhen, or heading to a scenic area in the mountains. The main thing we agree on is that we want a route with beautiful scenery, where we can stop whenever we feel like it, rather than following a fixed schedule. In terms of timing, I think we'd go during a long holiday, probably in the summer, when the weather is good for driving. We'd probably spend two or three days on the road, staying in small towns along the way. Since neither of us has done this kind of trip before, we'd need to plan it carefully, like booking hotels in advance and checking the car. The reason I want to go by car is that it gives you a sense of freedom that other transport can't offer. You can change your plans at any moment, pull over to enjoy a view, and carry whatever you need. I also think it would be a great way to spend quality time with my girlfriend, away from the busy city life. So even though we haven't fixed the details yet, I'm really looking forward to making this trip happen.

讲的是想和女朋友开车去的一次旅行，自己从没体验过。和谁去：女朋友，我们都喜欢一起旅行，聊过好几次这个想法。去哪：还没定具体目的地，讨论过几个选项，比如沿着深圳附近的海岸开，或者去山里的风景区；共识是想要风景好的路线，想停就停，不按固定行程走。什么时候：长假期间，大概夏天，天气适合开车；路上花两三天，沿途住小镇；因为都没经验，需要提前规划，比如订酒店、检查车况。为什么开车：开车给人其他交通方式给不了的自由感，随时能改计划、停下来看风景、带想带的东西；也是和女朋友远离城市忙碌生活、好好相处的机会。虽然细节还没定，但很期待成行。

Q2Which form of vehicle is more popular in your country, bikes, cars or motorcycles?

I think cars are the most popular form of vehicle in my country, especially in recent years, because more and more families can afford them. In big cities, however, bikes and electric bikes are also very common for short trips, since they're cheap and easy to park. Motorcycles are less popular in cities, mainly because of traffic restrictions, but they're still widely used in smaller towns and rural areas. So I'd say cars dominate overall, but bikes play a big role in daily city life.

我国最普及的交通工具是汽车，尤其近几年越来越多家庭买得起。不过大城市里自行车和电动车短途出行也很常见，便宜又好停；摩托车在城市里因限行不太流行，但在小城镇和农村仍广泛使用。总体汽车占主导，但自行车在城市日常生活中作用很大。

Q3Do you think air pollution comes mostly from mobile vehicles?

I think vehicles are a major source of air pollution, but not necessarily the biggest one in every place. In big cities, car exhaust definitely contributes a lot to smog, especially during rush hours. However, in many areas, factories and power plants produce even more pollution than vehicles. So I'd say vehicles are one of the main causes, but the situation depends on the region. In my country, the government has been promoting electric vehicles partly for this reason.

机动车是空气污染的主要来源之一，但不一定是每个地方最大的来源。大城市里汽车尾气确实对雾霾贡献很大，尤其高峰时段；但很多地区工厂和发电厂产生的污染比机动车还多。所以机动车是主因之一，但要看地区。我国政府推广电动车部分就是为了这个原因。

Q4Do you think people need to change the way of transportation drastically to protect the environment?

I think some change is necessary, but it doesn't have to be drastic all at once. Encouraging people to use public transport, walk or cycle more would already make a big difference in cities. Promoting electric vehicles is another practical step, since they produce much less pollution than petrol cars. That said, completely changing how everyone travels would be very difficult, because many people depend on cars for work and family reasons. So I'd say gradual but steady changes are more realistic than a sudden revolution.

改变是必要的，但不一定要一下子大改。鼓励人们多坐公共交通、步行或骑车，在城市里就能带来很大不同；推广电动车是另一个实际步骤，比汽油车污染少得多。不过彻底改变所有人的出行方式很难，因为很多人因工作和家庭原因离不开车。渐进但稳定的改变比突然的革命更现实。

Q5How are the transportation systems in urban areas and rural areas different?

The differences are quite significant. In urban areas, there are usually well-developed systems, like subways, buses and taxis, so people can get around easily without a car. Rural areas, on the other hand, often have limited public transport, with only a few buses running each day, so people rely heavily on private vehicles or motorcycles. Roads in rural areas may also be narrower and less well maintained. I think this gap is one reason why people in the countryside feel they need their own vehicle.

差异很明显。城市通常有发达的系统，如地铁、公交、出租车，没车也能方便出行；农村公共交通有限，每天只有几班公交，所以人们严重依赖私家车或摩托车；农村道路也可能更窄、维护更差。这个差距正是农村人觉得需要自己买车的原因之一。

Q6Why do more people own and drive private vehicles now?

I think the main reason is that cars have become more affordable, so owning one is no longer a luxury for most families. Rising incomes mean more people can buy a car, and many see it as a necessity for convenience, especially for commuting or taking children to school. Public transport can also be crowded and time-consuming, which pushes people towards driving. On top of that, in some areas, having a car is almost expected for social reasons. So I'd say affordability and convenience are the two biggest factors.

主要原因是汽车变得更便宜，对大多数家庭来说拥有汽车不再是奢侈品。收入增长让更多人买得起车，很多人把它看作便利的必需品，尤其通勤或接送孩子；公共交通又挤又耗时，也推动人们开车。另外有些地方出于社交原因几乎默认要有车。可负担性和便利性是两个最大因素。

Q7What do you think of the future of electric cars?

I think electric cars will become the mainstream in the future, and this is already happening in my country. They're cheaper to run than petrol cars, and they produce much less pollution, which fits the global push for cleaner energy. As battery technology improves, concerns about charging time and range will gradually disappear. That said, there are still challenges, like building enough charging stations and recycling old batteries. On the whole, I'm quite optimistic that electric cars will dominate the market within a decade or two.

我认为电动车未来会成为主流，我国已经在发生。它们比汽油车运行成本低，污染少得多，符合全球清洁能源的趋势；随着电池技术进步，充电时间和续航的顾虑会逐渐消失。不过仍有挑战，比如建足够的充电站、回收旧电池。总体我很乐观，一二十年内电动车会主导市场。
